title: Grateful Dead Live at Yale Bowl, Yale University on 1971-07-31
lineage: AKG 190E mic > Uher 4000 Report-L 5inch Reel > CD > EAC > WAV > SHN

ai_review.summary: Audience recording plagued by loud crowd screams, yet it captures the legendary July 31 1971 Yale Bowl show with a monster Dark Star and standout Pigpen moments.
ai_review.review: The tape is an audience (AUD) capture whose biggest flaw is the intrusive crowd noise – especially the scream that opens Dark Star – but once past those peaks the music shines.  The performance is high‑energy, featuring a long, soaring Dark Star, a beautiful Bird Song, the first‑ever Sugaree and a fiery Pigpen “Big Boss Man”, making it a must‑hear despite its technical shortcomings.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers praise the musical performance (many 4–5 star comments) while consistently noting crowd‑noise issues; weighted average of strong show quality and fair recording yields a solid 4‑star rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crowd screams dominate the mix, especially at the start of Dark Star; mid‑level frequencies are a bit off and occasional chatter masks instruments, but overall the recording remains listenable once volume is managed.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Early‑70s setlist with strong sequencing; Dark Star anchors the show, followed by tight jams and a surprising drop into Bird Song that keeps momentum high despite external chaos.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for ample space to work during Dark Star and overall guitar brilliance.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill (drums) noted as coming through instrumentally despite the audience mix.
